docs.title: Cocolit
docs.text:
Count coconut trees from satellite imagery. Draw a box on the map, and a YOLO11n detection model (Ultralytics, AGPL-3.0) marks every coconut tree inside it.

Live: cocolit.prithvilabs.com · Source: github.com/davnish/cocolit

docs.title: What it does
docs.text:
• Draw to detect: press Draw a box and drag (mouse or finger) over up to 0.5 km². A live tooltip shows the area while you draw.
  • Try another location: jump between dense coconut areas in Sri Lanka, India and Mexico.
  • Every tree marked: each detected coconut tree is drawn on the map, with the count, area and trees per km² for your session.
  • Coordinates bar: shows the pointer or map-centre position. Click the map to pin a point and copy it.
  • Statistics: every scan is saved in PostGIS and summarised as a heatmap and a per-country table.

docs.title: How it is built
docs.text:
A FastAPI frontend serves the map and calls a separate inference API, which streams satellite tiles into memory and runs the model with onnxruntime while the tiles are still downloading. Both run on a single k3s node behind a Cloudflare Tunnel, with Cloud Run taking requests when the node is busy.

Area Inference time Peak memory 0.1 km² 0.21 s 263 MB 1 km² 1.40 s 365 MB 2.5 km² 3.08 s 525 MB

Measured on an Apple M1, CPU only.

See Architecture for the full design: components, request flow, inference pipeline, database, deployment, configuration and where to change things.

docs.title: Run it locally
docs.text:
pip install -r requirements_inference.txt -r requirements_streamlit.txt
uvicorn src.api.inference:app --port 8000
INFERENCE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8000/predict uvicorn main:app --port 8501

Then open http://localhost:8501.

docs.title: License
docs.text: The code is MIT licensed. The model weights (models/best.onnx) are YOLO11n by Ultralytics and are AGPL-3.0. Satellite imagery is © Google.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
Cocolit counts coconut trees in satellite imagery. A user draws a box on a map, a YOLO11n model detects the trees inside it, and the result is drawn on the map and saved to a spatial database.

This page describes how the system is built and deployed, how a request flows through it, and where to make changes.

docs.title: System overview
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    user([Browser]) -->|HTTPS| cf[Cloudflare<br/>DNS, TLS, rate limit]
    cf -->|Tunnel, outbound only| fe

    subgraph k3s["k3s node · Helm release 'cocolit' · namespace 'apps'"]
        cfd[cloudflared] -.-> fe
        fe[Frontend<br/>main.py + static/] -->|1. local first| inf[Inference API<br/>src/api/inference.py]
        fe --> db[(PostGIS<br/>CloudNativePG)]
    end

    fe -.->|2. if local is busy or down| run[Cloud Run<br/>same inference image]
    inf --> tiles[(Google satellite tiles<br/>zoom 19)]
    run --> tiles
Component Code Runs as Job Frontend main.py, static/, src/inference_router.py Deployment cocolit-streamlit-deployment, port 8501 Serves the map UI; validates boxes; routes inference; saves results; statistics Inference API src/api/inference.py, pipelines/inference.py, src/utils/ Deployment cocolit-inference-server, port 8000 Downloads imagery for a box, runs the model, returns tree points as GeoJSON Database src/database/, src/dal/ CloudNativePG Cluster postgis-cluster Stores boxes, detected trees and low-confidence candidates for feedback Tunnel chart cloudflared_deployment.yaml Deployment cocolit-cloudflared Outbound connection to Cloudflare; the node needs no open inbound ports Overflow same inference image Cloud Run service cocolit-inference Takes requests when the local inference pod is busy or down; scales to zero

The deployment names keep their historical streamlit prefix; the frontend is no longer Streamlit.

docs.title: Frontend
docs.text:
main.py is a FastAPI app with three jobs:

  • Serve the UI. static/index.html, static/style.css and static/js/app.js are mounted at /. The UI is vanilla JavaScript with Leaflet (maps), Turf.js (live area) and Leaflet.heat (heatmap). At build time, frontend.Dockerfile stamps a version into the JS/CSS URLs because Cloudflare caches those files for hours.
  • Run inference (POST /api/inference): validate the drawn shape, ask the router for predictions, save them and return them in EPSG:4326.
  • Statistics (GET /api/statistics): totals, a per-country table and heatmap points for every saved detection.

It also exposes GET /healthz for Kubernetes probes and creates any missing database tables on startup.

docs.title: Drawing a box (static/js/app.js)
docs.text:
The box tool uses pointer events, so mouse, touch and pen share one code path:

  1. Draw a box turns on draw mode and disables map panning and zooming, so a drag draws instead of moving the map.
  2. pointerdown records the start corner, and pointermove resizes the rectangle and updates a tooltip with the live area. The tooltip turns red above 0.5 km².
  3. pointerup finishes the box; a tap (under 10 px of movement) is ignored. Boxes over 0.5 km² are rejected in the browser. Otherwise the GeoJSON is posted to /api/inference.
  4. Each detected tree is drawn as a small circle. The status line above the map reports the result, or an error such as a rate limit (429) or an invalid box (422).

Try another location cycles through SPOTS in app.js: dense coconut areas, each verified by running the model there, with village names from OpenStreetMap reverse geocoding.

docs.title: Local-first routing (src/inference_router.py)
docs.text:
InferenceRouter.predict() decides where each request runs:

  • If fewer than INFERENCE_MAX_LOCAL requests are in flight locally (default 1), the request goes to the local inference service.
  • If local is already busy, it goes straight to the overflow URL (Cloud Run) instead of queueing.
  • If local fails with a connection error, a timeout, or a 502/503/504, the request is retried once on overflow. Other errors (for example 422, box too big) are raised and not retried.
  • Without an overflow URL, everything goes to local.

The response header X-Inference-Backend: local|overflow shows which one served the request. Blocking work (HTTP and geopandas) runs in a thread via asyncio.to_thread, so one slow request doesn't freeze the frontend.

docs.title: Inference API
docs.text: src/api/inference.py exposes POST /predict (body: {xmin, ymin, xmax, ymax} in degrees) and GET /health. If INFERENCE_API_KEY is set (it is on Cloud Run), /predict requires a matching X-Api-Key header. Boxes that are too large or too small return 422.

docs.title: Pipeline (pipelines/inference.py)
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    participant API as /predict
    participant P as InferencePipeline.run
    participant T as tiles.stream_patches
    participant G as Google tiles
    participant M as OnnxDetector

    API->>P: BBox (degrees)
    P->>P: validate (625 m² to 5 km²)
    P->>T: MosaicPlan for the box
    T->>G: fetch all tiles, 16 at a time, row by row
    loop each row of 640 px patches, as soon as its tiles have arrived
        T-->>P: patches (BGR, zero-padded at the edges)
        P->>M: patch
        M-->>P: boxes + confidence
        P->>P: box centres → EPSG:3857 metres
    end
    P-->>API: Predictions → GeoJSON FeatureCollection
  • Tiles (src/utils/tiles.py). MosaicPlan.for_bounds() works out which zoom-19 tiles cover the box and how they crop to the box exactly, using the same maths and rounding as the earlier rasvec GeoTIFF pipeline. _download() fetches and decodes tiles concurrently into one uint8 canvas. stream_patches() yields each row of 640 × 640 patches as soon as the tiles under it have landed, so the model starts while later tiles are still downloading. A missing tile (404) stays black; other HTTP errors fail the request.
  • Model (src/utils/detector.py). OnnxDetector runs models/best.onnx on onnxruntime and reproduces Ultralytics' pre- and post-processing: BGR→RGB, scale to 0–1, confidence above 0.25, NMS at IoU 0.7, boxes clipped to the patch. Its output matches Ultralytics exactly, without PyTorch in the image.
  • Output. Box centres are mapped from patch pixels to EPSG:3857 metres and returned as a GeoJSON FeatureCollection with a conf property. An empty result is an empty FeatureCollection, not an error.
  • Telemetry. Every stage (validate, detect, postprocess) is timed into bbox.timings and recorded as an OpenTelemetry span and histogram. tile_wait and model split the detect time between waiting for tiles and running the model. The calls are no-ops until src/telemetry.py is wired in.

The model card and its AGPL-3.0 licence are in models/README.md.

docs.title: Performance
docs.text:
scripts/benchmark_inference.py, Apple M1, identical detections before and after:

Area Earlier (rasvec GeoTIFFs + Ultralytics) Now Peak RSS 0.1 km² 0.38 s 0.21 s 263 MB 1 km² 1.70 s 1.40 s 365 MB 2.5 km² 4.52 s 3.08 s 525 MB 4.9 km² 8.04 s 5.9 s 723 MB

About 70% of the time is now the model itself. The next speed-ups are an INT8 model (1.8× faster but only 90–96% agreement with FP32, so it needs validating on labelled data), batched inference (which needs a dynamic-batch export from the original .pt weights), and a cache for repeated areas.

docs.title: Database
docs.text:
PostGIS on CloudNativePG; tables are SQLModel classes in src/database/model.py, created on frontend startup.

erDiagram
    BoundingBox ||--o{ Pred : contains
    BoundingBox ||--o{ Feedback : has
    Pred ||--o| Feedback : "low confidence"
    BoundingBox {
        int id PK
        string datetime
        geometry geometry "POLYGON, EPSG:3857"
    }
    Pred {
        int id PK
        int id_bbox FK
        float conf
        geometry geometry "POINT, EPSG:3857"
    }
    Feedback {
        int id PK
        int id_pred FK
        int id_bbox FK
        int yes
        int no
    }
  • preds_bbox_to_database() saves a box with all its trees. Trees with confidence below 0.3 also get a Feedback row, collecting candidates for review and retraining. A box with no trees is not stored, because the box is saved through its predictions.
  • read_data() loads every prediction and joins it with the country boundaries in data/countries/ in Python. That's fine at the current size; for larger data, move the aggregation into PostGIS (for example ST_Within with a GROUP BY).

docs.title: Kubernetes (Helm chart infra/charts/cocolit)
docs.text:
Template Creates Enabled by inference_deployment.yaml, inference_service.yaml Inference pod and ClusterIP service (probes on /health, 1 Gi memory limit, no CPU limit) always streamlit_deployment.yaml, streamlit_service.yaml Frontend pod and service (probes on /healthz) always postgis_manifest.yaml, postgres-secret.yaml CloudNativePG cluster and credentials always (needs the CNPG operator) cloudflared_deployment.yaml Tunnel connector cloudflared.enabled inference_hpa.yaml Autoscaler inference.hpa.enabled (off for one node) streamlit_ingress.yaml, clusterissuer.yaml Traefik ingress and Let's Encrypt ingress.enabled, clusterIssuer.enabled (off behind the tunnel)
  • values.yaml holds the defaults.
  • values-laptop.yaml is the current single-node setup: k3s on Colima with locally built images (pullPolicy: Never), the tunnel on, ingress and cert-manager off, and a multi-arch PostGIS image.
  • Credentials come from a gitignored secrets-laptop.yaml. The tunnel token and the overflow URL and key are Kubernetes secrets created outside the chart.

scripts/deploy_laptop.sh builds both images and runs helm upgrade --install, using a Helm container if helm isn't installed.

docs.title: Edge: Cloudflare
docs.text:
• DNS for prithvilabs.com; the apex and www redirect to cocolit.prithvilabs.com.
  • The published tunnel route maps cocolit.prithvilabs.com to http://cocolit-streamlit-service.apps.svc.cluster.local:80.
  • A WAF rate-limiting rule on /api/inference allows 10 requests per 10 s per IP, then blocks for 10 s.

docs.title: Overflow: Cloud Run
docs.text:
scripts/deploy_cloud_run.sh:

  • builds the inference image for amd64 with Cloud Build and pushes it to Artifact Registry, keeping the newest 2 images;
  • deploys it with 1 vCPU, 1 GiB, concurrency 1, min-instances 0, max-instances 2 and an API key;
  • writes the URL and key into the inference-overflow secret. Turn it on with --set overflow.enabled=true.

docs.title: Target node: Oracle Cloud
docs.text: infra/oci/ is OpenTofu for an Always Free Ampere A1 VM (arm64). It sets up a VCN that only allows SSH from one IP, a separate data volume mounted at k3s's storage path (so the database survives replacing the node), and k3s installed by cloud-init. retry-apply.sh retries until Oracle has capacity.

docs.title: Images
docs.text:
Image Dockerfile Contents Size (compressed) Inference inference.Dockerfile onnxruntime, NumPy, Pillow, httpx, FastAPI, the model ≈111 MB Frontend frontend.Dockerfile FastAPI, geopandas, SQLModel/GeoAlchemy2, psycopg 3, static UI ≈160 MB

Both use only pure wheels (no compilers or GDAL), run as UID 10001, and build for arm64 and amd64.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
Variable Service Purpose INFERENCE_URL frontend Local inference endpoint (set by the chart) INFERENCE_OVERFLOW_URL frontend Cloud Run /predict URL; unset = no overflow INFERENCE_API_KEY both Shared secret; the frontend sends it, inference requires it if set INFERENCE_MAX_LOCAL frontend Concurrent local requests before overflowing (default 1) POSTGRES_HOST, POSTGRES_DATABASE, POSTGRES_USERNAME, POSTGRES_PASSWORD frontend Database connection (or local_database with a full URL); unset = no database SMTP_FROMADDR, SMTP_TOADDRS, SMTP_USERNAME, SMTP_PASSWORD frontend Error emails ORT_THREADS inference onnxruntime intra-op threads (default: all cores) PORT inference Listen port (Cloud Run sets it; default 8000) OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT both Enables OpenTelemetry export once wired in (otel.endpoint in the chart)

configs/config.yml sets the model path (model.path) and the number of concurrent tile downloads (inference.tile_workers, default 16).

docs.title: Where to change things
docs.text: To change… Edit Page text, layout, sections static/index.html Colours, spacing, mobile layout static/style.css (palette in the :root variables) Drawing, size limit in the UI, marker colours, status messages, featured locations (SPOTS) static/js/app.js API routes, validation, saving main.py When requests overflow to Cloud Run src/inference_router.py, overflow.maxLocal in the chart Box size limits (server) BBox.valid_bbox() in src/data_struct/bbox.py Tile source, zoom, download concurrency src/utils/tiles.py, configs/config.yml Detection thresholds (confidence, NMS) OnnxDetector in src/utils/detector.py The model replace models/best.onnx (same 1×3×640×640 input) and update models/README.md Tables and stored fields src/database/model.py, src/dal/preds.py Resources, probes, optional components infra/charts/cocolit/values*.yaml and templates

docs.title: Testing
docs.text:
pytest tests --ignore=tests/integration      # unit tests, no network
pytest tests/integration                      # real tiles + model (network)
python -m scripts.benchmark_inference --sizes 0.1 0.5 1 2.5

The unit tests cover:

  • tile placement, cropping and georeferencing against the rasvec formulas;
  • streaming patches matching the download-then-slice result;
  • conversion from pixels to map coordinates;
  • empty results;
  • GeoJSON parity with geopandas;
  • routing and overflow decisions;
  • API key checks and 422 responses.
